1.q: In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam
1.note: This refers to the eighteenth year of Jeroboam’s reign as king. Alternate translation: [In the eighteenth year that Jeroboam was king] or [in year 18 of King Jeroboam’s reign] (See also: [Ordinal Numbers](ta:translate-ordinal))

2.q: Macaiah, the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah
2.note: “Macaiah” is the name of a woman. “Uriel” is the name of a man.

2.q: There was war between Abijah and Jeroboam
2.note: The names of the kings represent the armies that they led. Alternate translation: [There was war between the army of Abijah and the army of Jeroboam]

3.note: “Four hundred thousand chosen men … eight hundred thousand chosen men.” The phrase “chosen men” is an idiom that refers to elite soldiers who were skilled in battle. Alternate translation: [400,000 skilled men … 800,000 skilled men] (See also: [Idiom](ta:figs-idiom))

5.q: Do you not know … by a formal covenant?
5.note: Abijah asks this rhetorical question to emphasize the positive answer that it anticipates. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this question as a statement. Alternate translation: [You know very well … by a formal covenant.]

8.note: This is a reference to a united Israel as it existed in the time of David and Solomon.

8.q: that is held within the hand of the descendants of David
8.note: Here the word “hand” represents authority and possession. Abijah is claiming that only the descendants of David have the rightful authority to rule Yahweh’s kingdom. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [that the descendants of David hold within their hand] or [which only the descendants of David have the authority to rule] (See also: [Active or Passive](ta:figs-activepassive))

8.q: the golden calves that Jeroboam made
8.note: It might be best to translate so that the reader understands that Jeroboam had others make the golden calves. Alternate translation: [the golden calves that Jeroboam had his craftsmen make]

9.q: But did you not drive out … as the people of other lands do?
9.note: Abijah asks this rhetorical question to rebuke the people and to emphasize the positive answer that it anticipates. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this question as a statement. Alternate translation: [But you drive out … as the people of other lands do.]

9.q: Whoever comes to serve as a priest
9.note: Alternate translation: [Anyone who comes to serve as a priest]

9.q: a priest of what are not gods
9.note: The phrase “what are not gods” refers to the golden calves that Jeroboam had his craftsmen make. Although the priests served them as if they were gods, they were not really gods. Alternate translation: [a priest of idols that are not really gods]

10.note: The word “us” refers to the people of the southern kingdom of Judah.
The word “work” can be translated with a verb. Alternate translation: [who are working]

11.note: The “bread of the presence” refers to twelve loaves of bread that the priests placed on a golden table in the tabernacle or temple building as a sacrifice to God and as a symbol of God’s presence.
Alternate translation: [they also take care of the lampstand]

11.q: for them to burn every evening
11.note: Alternate translation: [so that the lamps burn every evening] or [and light the lamps every evening]

12.q: God is with us at our head
12.note: Here the front of the army is spoken of as if it were the head. Abijah is saying that God is the one who is leading the army of Judah in battle. Alternate translation: [God is with us as our leader]
Since Yahweh is leading the army of Judah, Abijah speaks of the army of Israel fighting against the army of Judah as if they were fighting against Yahweh himself.

13.note: Alternate translation: [a surprise attack behind the army of Judah]
Alternate translation: [the soldiers who were to attack them by surprise were behind them]

14.note: Here “Judah” represents the soldiers in the army of Judah. Alternate translation: [When the soldiers of Judah looked back]
The word “behold” here shows that the soldiers were surprised by what they saw.

14.q: the fighting was both in front of them and behind them
14.note: The word “fighting” can be translated as a verb. Alternate translation: [the army of Israel was fighting them from the front and from the back]

15.q: God struck Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah
15.note: God enabling the army of Judah to defeat Jeroboam and the army of Israel is spoken of as if God struck Jeroboam and Israel. Alternate translation: [God enabled Abijah and the army of Judah to defeat Jeroboam and all Israel]
Here the word “Israel” refers to the army. Alternate translation: [the entire army of Israel]

16.note: Here the word “Judah” represents the army of Judah. Alternate translation: [fled before the army of Judah]

16.q: God gave them into the hand of Judah
16.note: Here the word “hand” represents power. God enabling the army of Judah to defeat the army of Israel is spoken of as if God had put the army of Israel in the hand of the army of Judah. Alternate translation: [God enabled Judah to defeat the people of Israel] (See also: [Metaphor](ta:figs-metaphor))

17.note: This idiom means that they thoroughly defeated them, or that they killed very many of the soldiers. Alternate translation: [thoroughly defeated them] or [slaughtered many of their soldiers]

“five hundred thousand chosen men.” The phrase “chosen men” is an idiom that refers to elite soldiers who were skilled in battle. Alternate translation: [500,000 of the best soldiers] (See also: [Idiom](ta:figs-idiom))

18.q: the people of Israel were subdued
18.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the army of Judah subdued the people of Israel]

19.note: These are the names of cities.

20.q: Yahweh struck him, and he died
20.note: Yahweh causing Jeroboam to die is spoken of as if Yahweh struck Jeroboam. It is possible that this refers to Yahweh causing Jeroboam to become ill. Alternate translation: [Yahweh caused Jeroboam to die] or [Yahweh caused Jeroboam to become ill, and he died] (See also: [Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information](ta:figs-explicit))

21.q: he took fourteen wives for himself
21.note: The idiom “took … wives” means that he married. Alternate translation: [he married fourteen women]

21.q: fourteen wives … twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters

22.note: Alternate translation: [his behavior, and his sayings] or [his behavior, and the things that he said]

22.q: are written in the history of the prophet Iddo
22.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [are in the history that the prophet Iddo wrote]
